theMechanismFoundInTheCode.whereTheWrongRetirementIsBorn: artifacts/api-server/src/lib/nodeFacetBakeTier1Conformant.ts:1336-1358. `cadPropRow = input.cadPropertyRoll.byPropId.get(apn)`, then `recordRetirement = apn != null && cadPropConsulted && cadPropRow == null`. The roll the builder is handed is NOT the raw declared-vintage roll: nodeFacetBakeTier1ConformantCli.ts:544-591 (P-177, 2026-09-13) replaces it with `effectiveCadPropertyRoll`, a REMAPPED view keyed by the node's own bare prop_id whose entry is the CAD account the node's own published geo_id names (or NO ENTRY when the crosswalk cannot name one).
theMechanismFoundInTheCode.theConflation: After P-177 there are TWO different statements that both arrive at the builder as `cadPropRow == null`: (1) the node's account WAS named and is genuinely absent from the declared roll -- a real retirement; and (2) the node's account could NOT BE NAMED AT ALL, so nothing was looked up. The retirement predicate reads both as (1). That is the defect this row exists to fix, and it is one sentence: a lookup that did not happen is not a lookup that came back empty.

theDollarCollisionQuestionAnswered.question: does a Hays map-id node that collides with an unrelated account get that account's dollars today?
theDollarCollisionQuestionAnswered.measured: 134,907 of Hays' 173,050 served nodes carry a bare key that IS also a `cad_property` prop_id at the declared 2026 vintage (P-177's collision population). 77,565 of those serve a market value.
theDollarCollisionQuestionAnswered.answer: NO -- not for 77,553 of them. Served `baseFacts.cadRoll.marketValue.v` equals the colliding account's own `market_value` on only 12 rows, and on all 12 the node's OWN R account carries the identical figure, so the agreement is a value coincidence and not a wrong-parcel read. P-177's account-attribute crosswalk already covers this; what it does not cover is the retirement predicate, which is this row.

legacyDesignTools: src/lib/retirementAccountResolution.ts (NEW). The one resolution, pure and dependency-free like joinNormalize.ts. A node's retirement resolution is one of: `own-prop-id` (a non-blocked county, where the bare key IS the account -- the legacy path, unchanged); `crosswalk-geo-id-bind` (the node's own published geo_id names the account's property_number, corroborated by the account's own account-number stem -- the SAME `accountCrosswalkForNode` P-177 already uses, reused and not re-derived); `r-account-register` (the node's own key IS the county's published R-account number, matched as the exact published identifier `R<key>`, and admissible ONLY when the node's own geo_id is absent or names the same property_number); `published-account-pair` (an injected map of published node key -> account key, built by the CLI from the county's own staged extracts); or `unresolved` with a named reason (no-published-identifier / no-account-publishes-it / ambiguous-property-number / corroboration-refused / contradiction).

src/lib/nodeFacetBakeTier1Conformant.ts (EDIT). `ConformantTier1BuildInput` gains one OPTIONAL field, `retirementResolution`. When it is absent the builder computes exactly what it computes today (key = apn, path = own-prop-id) -- which is what keeps a non-blocked county byte-identical. When it is present: `cadPropRow` is looked up by the resolution's accountKey (so the DOLLARS ride the same resolution, as the dispatch requires), the retirement is earned ONLY for a resolved account that is absent from the roll, and a resolution that is `unresolved` writes `recordRetirement: null` PLUS a declared `retirementResolution` (verdict, path, the served key, the account key, the served keyspace, the roll keyspace, the roll's tax year, the reason, an authority, a scope, an asOf and a per-parcel basis) so the payload says the retirement could not be determined and why. `recordRetirement` is emitted only when `isEarnedRecordRetirement` still accepts it; the retirement's own authority/basis name the ACCOUNT the arm compared, not the node's bare key.

src/lib/accountKeyedWork.ts (EDIT). The blast-radius instrument for writer (b): a pure `accountKeyedBlastRadius` that takes the excluded set and the served keyspaces the caller measured, and refuses when the excluded set IS a whole served keyspace (P-327's suggested shape). With a test that proves the refusal fires and names the keyspace.

src/nodeFacetBakeTier1ConformantCli.ts (EDIT). Builds the per-node resolution for a gate-blocked county from the reads it ALREADY does (crosswalkKeyByPropId / accountStemByPropId / accountCrosswalkForNode) plus ONE new indexed read: the declared-vintage `quick_ref_id` register, and -- only to name an account the declared vintage no longer carries -- the prior vintage's register. Threads the resolution into the builder. Calls the writer-(b) instrument before the pass and REFUSES the run when it fires. Prints one counter per resolution path, so a run that resolves nothing is visible in the log.

theWriterBDecision.ruled: Writer (b) STAYS IN THE BAKE'S CONTRACT, and gets its own instrument.
why: It cannot belong to the gate. It runs INSIDE the bake, after promotion, on the work list the bake built and the run stamp the bake minted; the factory's pre-bake gate (`requireRetirementGate` in runBastropPublish) runs before the bake exists and cannot see a single excluded node. Moving it to the gate is not a refactor, it is a different program.

It must not be DROPPED either: a node dropped from the work list keeps the previous run's publishRunId forever, and the factory's verify-walk requires the CURRENT run id on every row it sweeps, an earned retirement included (accountKeyedWork.ts:22-50). Dropping the pass re-opens BP-PUBLISH-RUN-01 on every Hays republish.

So the pass stays, and the thing it lacks is the guard every other destructive write in this program lacks (the program trap: 'No writer in this program refuses on blast radius yet (P-320)'). That guard is writer (b)'s instrument.

HONEST LIMIT, stated now rather than discovered later: this instrument guards writer (b) ONLY. It would NOT have caught the Williamson emptying, which was writer (a) -- the excluded set there was empty, because every removed node was in the parcel table. Writer (a)'s guard is the resolution itself (a node whose account cannot be named is not retired), and that is a different instrument in a different file. Claiming the blast-radius guard covers both would be exactly the 'a control that measures one thing does not protect the thing beside it' failure the program trap names.
theWriterBDecision.theInstrument: Before the retirement pass, the CLI measures the excluded set against the served keyspaces it read (the county's served tier-1 keys, grouped into keyspaces by the caller's own classifier) and REFUSES the run when the excluded set IS a whole served keyspace -- i.e. when a keyspace has at least one served member and every one of them was excluded. The refusal names the keyspace, the excluded count and the served count. Proven by a fixture in both directions: the whole-keyspace case refuses and writes nothing; the Hays case (a hollow subset of one keyspace) passes.

preRegisteredFalsifiers: F1 HAYS COLLISION: a node whose bare key equals an unrelated account number. On the PRE-change code the fixture node earns a `recordRetirement` (the colliding account's absence/mismatch reads as this node's retirement) and its `baseFacts.cadRoll` is the wrong parcel's or empty. On the fixed code it resolves through the R-account register, retires NOTHING, and carries the account its own published identifier names. Revert-and-run: the test is run against `git stash`ed pre-change source and must FAIL there.

F2 WILLIAMSON PAIR: an R node the pair reaches (must resolve to the numeric account, no retirement, and the account's facts) and one the pair does NOT reach (must NOT retire; must carry a declared retirementResolution naming the pair as the reason). Proven on the pre-change code in the first direction: the reached node retires wrongly.

F3 A GENUINE ACCOUNT RETIREMENT STILL RETIRES. A node whose ACCOUNT resolves and is absent from the declared roll must still earn an earned `recordRetirement` (the predicate is not weakened), and the retirement's authority must name the account it compared.

F4 AN UNRESOLVABLE KEY IS DECLARED, NOT RETIRED. `recordRetirement` must be null and the declared `retirementResolution` must carry a non-empty reason and a per-parcel basis (two parcels may not share a character-identical basis -- the same discipline every earned absence in this bake follows).

F5 BASTROP (AND EVERY NON-BLOCKED COUNTY) IS BYTE-IDENTICAL. A single-keyspace county's payload, built with no `retirementResolution`, must serialise to the same bytes as the pre-change builder. Proven by hashing the serialised payload before and after.

F6 THE WRITER-(B) INSTRUMENT FIRES ON A WHOLE KEYSPACE AND NOT OTHERWISE. A fixture whose excluded set is a whole served keyspace must refuse and name it; the measured Hays shape (a hollow subset) must pass. Would falsify: an instrument that refuses healthy churn, which is how a control gets disabled by its first real caller.
F7 THE KEYS-THAT-CANNOT-BE-NAMED ARE COUNTED, NOT ABSORBED. A run that resolves zero accounts must be visible: every resolution path has its own counter and the run prints them.

theThreeQuestionGateAsDesigned.whatExecutesEachWriter: (a) `buildConformantTier1Payload`'s retirement arm, called once per work item by `nodeFacetBakeTier1ConformantCli.ts`'s per-atom loop, reading `cadPropertyRoll`. (b) `planAccountKeyedRetirements` via `partitionAccountKeyedWork`, called on the CLI's work list for a gate-blocked county.
theThreeQuestionGateAsDesigned.whatTriggersThem: (a) a declared-vintage `cad_property` read plus a node whose resolved account the roll does not carry. (b) `joinGateBlocked && parcelTable` -- the account-keyed prepass, for every gate-blocked county, on every run.
theThreeQuestionGateAsDesigned.whatFailsWhenAWriterRetiresAcrossKeyspac: The county's published nodes are emptied: Williamson's 2026-09-17 run retired 282,570 of 282,570 R nodes while 319,480 live numeric rows sat untouched beside them, and Hays still serves 1,042 live parcels with a false retirement (810 admissible, 232 contradicted) plus 344 it cannot name.
whatBypassesIt: A direct invocation of the bake CLI (any run outside `runBastropPublish`) -- which is why writer (b)'s guard must live in the bake and not in the gate.
Writer (b)'s pass is bypassed structurally for any county whose work list already excludes the nodes before the pass could see them.

openQuestionsForTheIntegrationSeat: Whether the 810 Hays nodes that this lane un-retires should take their dollars from the R account the register names. This lane says yes (they are live parcels; the register is the county's own published account number and the node's own id IS that number), and it is stated as a change of served values on 810 rows rather than folded into the retirement fix without a word.

Whether the 232 contradicted nodes should be escalated to the county or left as declared absences. This lane leaves them declared; a bind that two published identifiers disagree about is not this lane's to resolve.
